# Kamunity MPA — extended public guide

The Kamunity programme groups its work into three connected product lines: community coordination (Kamunity AI and The Pack), signal-to-action infrastructure (including Phoenix Node and this MPA demonstration), and public/commercial entry (consulting and a small curated tool set).

The MPA is a public demonstration and navigation point, not the whole programme. Its selected pages present public news, rooms, tools, organisation-facing resources, a constitution and a way to contact Mike Fuller. The MPA does not need to replace the predecessor site at kamunity.org.

## What a visitor can do

- Browse public sector news and room briefs. These are sourced through bounded public feed paths; a visible card is not a substitute for checking its underlying source and editorial status.
- Use selected printable and browser-side tools, including the Corporate Volunteering Partnership Planner. The Compliance Harm Observations tool prepares an anonymised draft for human review, not a verified finding or legal advice.
- Explore the Warehouse catalogue, which distinguishes Kamunity resources from independent third-party services.
- Contact Mike at mike@kamunityconsulting.com. The MPA does not offer a contact form or public Kai chat in this release.

## Important boundaries

Kai is presented as a proposed AI wayfinder. Its public conversation endpoint is unavailable in this MPA release. The separate Reflection destination is an external sibling site and should be assessed on its own terms.

GGA material is retained as a historical example, not a currently offered live instance. Mycelium is a retired direction and is not recommended here. Bothy is primarily an internal approach, though its public explanatory page is included.

The selected third-party services are independent of Kamunity. Features, prices, data handling and suitability can change, so verify directly before adoption. Public tools and assessments are aids to discussion, not professional, clinical, legal or financial advice.

This guide describes the approved editorial scope. Final hosted link checks, live-feed checks and owner release acceptance remain separate.
